subject: Oceanography
title: Subduction Zones
description: A short lesson to help you apply Subduction Zones.

hook.text: Where ocean plates collide with continents, one plate dives beneath the other—into Earth's mantle.

buildup.text: The denser oceanic plate slides under the lighter continental plate in a process called subduction.

discovery.text: Subducting plates melt at depth, generating magma that rises to form volcanic arcs on the surface.

twist.text: The Andes, Japan's volcanoes, and the Cascades all sit above subduction zones.

climax.text: Subduction recycles ocean crust back into the mantle—completing the tectonic cycle.

punchline.text: Old ocean floor sinks, melts, and fuels volcanoes.

quiz.question: What happens to oceanic crust at a subduction zone?
options: It dives beneath another plate into the mantle
